Note on k — three distinct orders appear in this document.
• Projection order k = 1 — the order used to build Mkstride and the projection plane in Panel 5.
• Ladder-saturation order k = 6 — the smallest order at which log ρ(Ak) − log ρ(Ak+1) < 0.005, i.e. where the estimated candidate-graph entropy flattens.
• Last ladder order k = 6 — the largest order actually evaluated in the entropy ladder (Panel 10). The reported hk = ln ρ(Ak) is taken at this order.
These three values are not expected to coincide. The metrics card reports ρ(Ak) at the projection order; the ladder and the reported hk are evaluated at the largest ladder order. If the projection order is smaller, that is because the projection uses the tightest order, not the largest.

What is claimed, and what is not. This document analyses a finite word w and a family of empirical graphs built from its factors. A shift space XEOA is not defined here. The quantity hk = ln ρ(Ak) is the topological entropy of the sofic shift presented by the empirical graph Gk — a well-defined object built from w. It is not asserted to equal the topological entropy of any underlying system, in either direction: a posited XEOA could contain longer factors not observed in w, and could exclude factors that were observed. Possible constructions of XEOA (a limit sequence, an orbit closure, a substitution subshift, an S-adic system, a language shift, or an empirical finite-word system) are mathematically distinct and are not chosen here.

2. Input and Operator Disclosure

The terms EOA, LCR, and β-operator are specific to this project and are not standard in symbolic dynamics.

Input

The public artifact identifies the semantic input as the spoken English letter name “a”. The exact EOA phonetic encoding that is fed to the recursive operator is disclosed under collaboration access and is not reproduced here. A researcher reading this artifact can therefore reproduce everything reported below about the released word, but cannot independently regenerate that word from the semantic input without the encoding.

LCR (control parameter)

LCR denotes the limiting-ratio control parameter used by the EOA construction to determine the recursive transformation applied to the phonetic input. In this artifact, LCR is set to 3.14. The formal mathematical definition of LCR — and its role in the transformation — is part of the EOA technical documentation and is available to qualified collaborators under the stated agreement. It is not reproduced in this public artifact.

β-operator

The released sequence is generated by the EOA β-operator applied to the stated phonetic input and the LCR parameter above. The β-operator — including its exact transformation rules and implementation details — is available to qualified researchers under a signed collaboration agreement. The public artifact therefore provides complete reproducibility of the released word and its reported finite-word statistics, while full reproduction from the original phonetic input requires access to the β-operator. Researchers interested in examining or extending the construction may request access from the author through the collaboration portal.

Scope of what this document establishes

The present document analyzes a sequence generated by the EOA β-operator. The hash above confirms that the displayed analyses refer to one exact sequence. It does not independently prove that the sequence was produced by the claimed operator; such verification requires access to the operator itself.

Access

Requests for the β-operator, the exact phonetic encoding, or the full EOA technical documentation are handled through the following channel:

  • research.neurolabs.space
  • Request via the contact link on that site.
  • Availability is subject to a signed collaboration agreement (use, attribution, non-redistribution).

Model-dependent estimates

Three distinct objects are used in this document. They carry different spectral radii and are reported separately.

ObjectDefinitionUsed for
Mkstride Letter-level stride matrix: M[a,b] = #{ i : wi = a, wi+k = b }. Count-weighted. No normalisation. No inverse-frequency weighting. Empirical projection plane (Panel 5)
Gk Order-k factor-overlap graph: nodes = distinct order-k factors of w; edge (a1…ak) → (a2…ak+1) with observed count as edge weight. Subword transition graph (Panel 6); candidate graph growth (Panel 10)
Ak Binary adjacency matrix of Gk: Ak[u][v] = 1 if the transition u → v was observed, else 0. Edge weights of Gk are not used in the spectral calculation. Candidate graph entropy
ρ(Ak) Spectral radius of Ak, computed by power iteration (300 steps) on the binary adjacency structure. This is the standard object for a topological-entropy-like quantity; count weights would instead give a Parry-measure-like quantity, which is not what is reported here. Entropy calculation
hk hk = ln ρ(Ak), evaluated at the exact order k indicated. This is the topological entropy of the sofic shift presented by the empirical graph Gk. It is a well-defined number for that object. It is not asserted to equal the topological entropy of any underlying system, which is not defined in this document. Finite empirical graph statistic

Reported orders. The metrics card shows ρ(Ak) at the projection order k = 1. The candidate-graph entropy hk is reported at the last ladder order k = 6. The two numbers are different objects at different orders and are not expected to satisfy hk = ln ρ(Ak) across orders.

QuantityValueModel & order
ρ(Ak) — projection order 4.502045 ρ(Ak) at k = 1. Shown in the metrics card.
hk = ln ρ(Ak) — last ladder order 0.215173 hk = ln ρ(Ak) at k = 6. Topological entropy of the sofic shift presented by Gk. Not the entropy of any posited underlying system.
ρ(Mkstride) — projection order (shown in Panel 5) Spectral radius of the stride-k letter matrix Mkstride at k = 1. Not reported in this table because it is a different object.
hblock — finite-sample block-growth rate 0.221416 (1/n)·ln p(n) at n = nmax = min(30, max(6, ⌊|w|/6⌋)). Not an entropy estimate of the generating subshift; a finite-prefix observable.
Sofic–block gap -0.006243 → 0 if the empirical graph is memory-tight at the last ladder order.
Max prefix discrepancy 8.12 maxc|Nc(n) − n·πc| over observed prefixes.

These quantities are computed from the models described above. Each is a well-defined number for the empirical object named. None is asserted to equal the corresponding quantity for any underlying system. In particular, ρ(Ak) is not a Perron–Frobenius eigenvalue of a substitution.

Unresolved structural questions

The finite-word statistics are compatible with several structural regimes. Which one, if any, governs the underlying system is not determined by the analyses above.

Appendix 4.A — Model definitions

QuantityDefinition used in this artifact
Mkstride (letter-level stride matrix) Count-weighted letter-level matrix at stride k. Entry M[a,b] = number of positions i with wi = a and wi+k = b. Built from the released word only. No normalisation. No inverse-frequency weighting. This matrix is used only to build the projection plane in Panel 5.
Gk (factor-overlap graph) Nodes = distinct order-k factors of w. Edges = ordered pairs of overlapping order-k factors: (wi…wi+k−1) → (wi+1…wi+k). Edge weight = observed count. This graph is a presentation of a sofic shift containing the observed word, not of the generating subshift.
Ak (binary adjacency of Gk) Ak[u][v] = 1 if the transition u → v was observed in Gk, else 0. Edge weights from Gk are ignored for the spectral calculation; only the binary allowed-transition structure is used. This is the standard convention for a topological-entropy-like quantity.
ρ(Ak) Spectral radius of Ak, computed by power iteration (300 steps) on the binary adjacency structure. Reported in the estimates table (at the projection order) and in the entropy ladder (Panel 10, at every order 1 … 6).
ρ(Mkstride) Spectral radius of the stride-k letter matrix Mkstride. Shown in Panel 5 only. Distinct object from ρ(Ak); the two numbers are not expected to coincide.
hk (entropy of the empirical sofic presentation) hk = ln ρ(Ak). Reported with the exact order k used (here k = 6 for the value in the statistics section). This is the topological entropy of the sofic shift presented by the empirical graph Gk. It is a well-defined number for that object. It is not asserted to equal the topological entropy of any posited underlying system, which is not defined in this document.
Logarithm base Natural log (base e) throughout. hk = ln ρ(Ak); hblock = (1/n)·ln p(n).
n used for hblock nmax = min(30, max(6, ⌊|w|/6⌋)). The reported value is (1/n)·ln p(n) at the largest feasible n for this word, not an extrapolated limit.
Max prefix discrepancy maxc|Nc(n) − n·πc| where Nc(n) = count of symbol c in the prefix w1…wn, and πc = its frequency in the full released word. Computed over the first 10,000 symbols.

Appendix 4.B — Surrogate control definitions (Panel 12)

Single replicate shown; visual diagnostic only. Surrogates are seeded deterministically from a hash of the input word, so re-exporting the same sequence reproduces the same Panel 12.
freq-shuffle — uniform random permutation of w via a seeded Fisher–Yates. Preserves exact unigram counts; destroys all higher-order structure.
Markov order-1 — empirical order-1 Markov chain with P(b|a) = N(ab) / N(a), sampled with a seeded PRNG. Initial symbol fixed to w1. Length equals |w|.
periodic — first T symbols of w repeated, T = min(50, ⌊|w|/40⌋).

The single-replicate display above is a visual diagnostic, not a test. A statistically meaningful comparison would require replicate ensembles per surrogate (≳30 for a crude z-score, ≳200 for a stable empirical null) and multiple-testing control across the statistics shown. That apparatus is not implemented here.

Hash-check procedure.
  1. Download the full sequence using the link in Section 3.
  2. Compute SHA-256 over its UTF-8 bytes (whitespace stripped).
  3. Compare to the hash in Section 1.

If the hash matches, the sequence is bit-identical to the one analyzed here. All observed finite-word statistics (length, alphabet, factor counts) will then reproduce exactly. The model-dependent estimates reproduce when the same model and settings are used.

Panel images are rendered in-browser and may differ at the pixel level. The structure they depict is invariant; Panel 12 is seeded from the sequence and is reproducible.

Reproducibility

The released word, its SHA-256, its factor counts, and the displayed finite-word statistics are fully reproducible from the artifacts in this file alone. Full reconstruction of the released word from the phonetic input requires the β-operator and the exact phonetic encoding, both available under a signed collaboration agreement.
